evidence_items.source_text: A woman in her early 30s presented to the retina clinic with a progressive decrease in central vision in both eyes and metamorphopsia over 6 months. She had no significant past medical or ocular history, and she denied any history of trauma. On examination, the best-corrected visual acuity (OD) was 6/24, N8 (−3.50 dioptre sphere, −2.00 dioptre cylindrical, axis 10 degree) and (OS) was 4/60 (-4.00 dioptre sphere, −1.00 dioptre cylindrical, axis 180 degree). Examination with the Amsler grid chart revealed bilateral metamorphopsia. Anterior segment examination of both eyes was normal. She had a clear crystalline lens. The axial length was 24.02 mm (OD) and 24.15 mm (OS). The intraocular pressure was 14 mm Hg in both eyes. Fundoscopic examination revealed full-thickness macular holes in both eyes. The right eye showed a mild temporal peripapillary atrophy. No peripheral retinal breaks were seen. Spectral domain OCT (using the Topcon Maestro 2) was done, which confirmed the presence of FTMHs with cystic spaces in both eyes (figure 1a,b). The minimum inner diameter length of the MH was 431 µm (OD) and 512 µm (OS). Systemic evaluation included blood tests for autoimmune markers, infectious agents and metabolic disorders, all of which were unremarkable. Bilateral macular hole repair surgery was recommended, which she underwent 3 weeks later for the left eye and 7 weeks later for the right eye from the time of presentation.

The patient underwent a standard three-port 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy in the left eye first. After core vitrectomy, intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide was injected to stain posterior cortical vitreous and induce posterior vitreous detachment. Air–fluid exchange was done, and ILM was stained with brilliant blue green. ILM peeling was carried out about 2-disc diameters around the macular hole. A non-expansile mixture of 14% C3F8 Gas tamponade was given. The patient was asked to maintain a face-down position for 10 hours a day for 7 days. To minimise the risks associated with bilateral simultaneous surgery, the surgery for the right eye was performed 4 weeks later.

Postoperative visual acuity improved to 6/9 (OD) and 6/18p (OS) after 2 weeks. Fundus examination (OD) showed closure of the macular hole and temporal peripapillary atrophy (figure 2a). OCT (OD) demonstrated type 2A closure of the macular hole with restoration of the foveal contour (figure 2b). Fundus examination also showed closure of the macular hole (figure 2c). OCT (OS) demonstrated type 1B closure of the macular hole (figure 2d).

At the 10th weeks, the best corrected visual acuity improved to 6/9p, N6 (−3.50 dioptre sphere, −2.00 dioptre cylindrical, axis 10 degree) in OD and 6/9, N6 (−4.00 dioptre sphere, −1.00 dioptre cylindrical, axis 180 degree) in OS. The OCT still showed a type 2A closure (OD) and type 1B closure (OS) of the macular hole.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: Bilateral idiopathic macular hole in a young female
diagnostic_reasoning_verbatim_spans: Fundoscopic examination revealed full-thickness macular holes in both eyes. ... Spectral domain OCT (using the Topcon Maestro 2) was done, which confirmed the presence of FTMHs with cystic spaces in both eyes
Systemic evaluation included blood tests for autoimmune markers, infectious agents and metabolic disorders, all of which were unremarkable.

The aetiology of bilateral macular holes in this young patient remains unclear. While idiopathic causes are most likely, the absence of typical risk factors such as high myopia, trauma or vitreomacular traction is unusual.
